claims.statement: `FilesystemMiddleware` exposes an allowlisted filesystem tool surface, filters unsupported optional `delete` and `execute` capabilities from model requests, and separately applies request-time content lifecycle and per-call filesystem policy.

Filesystem permissions are enforced in tool implementations, whereas `interrupt` rules are compiled during graph assembly into HITL predicates; profile tool exclusions instead filter and reject tool names as a non-security model-surface control.

`CompositeBackend` routes a path to the longest matching prefix, strips that prefix for the delegated backend, remaps path-bearing results into the composite namespace, and lists virtual route directories alongside default-root entries at `/`.

For root-wide composite searches, `grep` shares one match budget across default and routed backends and conservatively marks skipped routes as truncated, while `glob` remaps results, preserves anchoring through route-pattern rewriting or skipping, and surfaces a searched backend error instead of a partial successful merge.

With `offload_binary_content=True`, FilesystemMiddleware replaces eligible read-file and human-media payloads in history with digest-addressed blob references, rehydrates verified data only for model requests, and disables offload when the blob route is state-backed.

`FilesystemBackend` virtual mode maps virtual absolute and relative paths under `root_dir`, rejects traversal and paths resolving outside that root, and hides the host root in agent-visible paths; it is path semantics rather than sandbox or process isolation.

Filesystem permission rules use first-match operation/path matching, deny either a requested path or its resolvable filesystem target, and reject an unresolvable target when rules are configured; recursive or ambiguous deletes additionally fail closed on overlapping deny patterns.

The generated HITL predicates distinguish exact from bulk filesystem calls: exact calls honor a preceding deny, while bulk calls interrupt when their search scope can overlap a protected anchor, treating omitted or current-directory paths as root and inspecting redirecting glob patterns.

Execution is available only through an execution-capable backend and a composite delegates it to its default backend; `execute` validates timeout limits and exposes a nonzero process exit as an artifact on a successful tool invocation, while `LocalShellBackend` executes arbitrary shell input on the host without isolation.
dcode composes SDK filesystem tools with caller-supplied tools and loaded MCP tools; MCP use adds timeout middleware and can be disabled before tool loading.

dcode’s tools catalog compiles the real agent with an offline placeholder model, forwards the filesystem allowlist, groups MCP tools by server, and exposes unavailable servers or generic discovery failure rather than silently omitting them.

dcode validates `allow_fs_tools` as an operational security allowlist and, for an explicit subset, replaces the main filesystem middleware and injects an equivalent restriction into raw subagents; it rejects compiled subagents that could bypass this enforcement.

dcode manages optional ripgrep by selecting system or verified managed binaries, downloading and hash-verifying a pinned platform artifact when necessary, and isolating a profile fallback binary through a private PATH shim rather than exposing its directory.

dcode’s file-operation tracker records backend-aware pre/post images for filesystem presentation, marks unavailable images as untrustworthy rather than fabricating diffs, preserves known write metrics after read-back failure, and redacts known sensitive filename patterns from display.

`GlobResult` can communicate a successful but incomplete search with a reason of budget, unreadable subtree, or transport clipping, while `ReadResult` validates pagination metadata so malformed windows fail before middleware presentation.

dcode server launch preflights an explicit MCP configuration, serializes resolved `ServerConfig` into server environment variables, scaffolds and starts a temporary LangGraph runtime, and only after graph readiness binds `RemoteAgent` to the workspace with a session-policy claim and its fingerprint; unhanded-off servers are reaped on failure or cancellation without blocking the event loop, with full graceful shutdown retained while sandbox startup may need cleanup.

`SandboxBackendProtocol` adds execution to the storage protocol, while `BaseSandbox` implements filesystem helpers on that command primitive and upload/download transport without adding isolation; its opt-in capture path can retain oversized output in the executing sandbox, and the local subprocess suite is gated behavioral coverage rather than a security boundary test.

The server accepts a workspace claim only when its exact session-policy payload and canonical fingerprint match the policy it resolved for the requested workspace; it rejects project-scoped claim fields, then binds the complete trusted workspace policy for the thread.

An explicit `ALLOW_FS_TOOLS` server environment value is fail-closed: it must be a non-empty JSON list of recognized names and must include `read_file`, so malformed or tampered values cannot silently enable the unrestricted filesystem default.
